Mechanism-centric cross-domain retrieval for scientific discovery: LLM agents for structural isomorphism beyond semantic similarity
abstract: Cross-domain isomorphisms, hidden shared structural patterns across disparate fields, are critical for driving interdisciplinary innovation. However, identifying these isomorphisms is difficult due to information overload and knowledge silos. This leaves numerous knowledge connections buried, constraining scientific discovery. To address these limitations, we propose the Mechanism-Centric Cross-Domain Retrieval Framework (MCDF), which integrates three core components: 1) an Expert-Guided Mechanistic Schema with a taxonomy of ten universal mechanism classes, driving 26 domain-specific reasoning agents to generate mechanistically equivalent keywords; 2) a Disentangled Dual-Evaluator architecture that adversarially scores Topic Relevance (TRS) and Mechanism Alignment (MAS) to eliminate metric contamination; and 3) the Isomorphic Serendipity Index (ISI), a novel ranking metric with a cross-domain gain term and a mechanism-gated rarity boost that mathematically incentivizes high mechanistic alignment coupled with maximal semantic distance. In two case studies (social rumor propagation and AI model collapse), MCDF retrieved high-fidelity mechanistic isomorphisms from diverse distant disciplines, average MAS > 0.82 (far higher than BM25 and Deep Research). Results from human evaluation and ablation studies further validate the framework’s effectiveness in enhancing discovery serendipity while maintaining structural validity. MCDF provides a scalable framework for automated cross-domain mining that activates latent knowledge resources to drive interdisciplinary innovation.

AMC-GPT: Integrating physics-informed interference emulation into Generative Pre-trained Transformers for AMC
Learning design skills as memory policies for agentic photonic inverse design
abstract: Photonic crystal fiber (PCF) inverse design remains challenging because candidate geometries must satisfy coupled optical targets under expensive electromagnetic simulation. Existing pipelines improve surrogate prediction or one-shot parameter recommendation, but they do not accumulate reusable design knowledge across iterative trials. We formulate PCF inverse design as a memory-policy learning problem and propose SkillPCF, a closed-loop agent framework that combines a physics-guided memory skill bank, reinforcement-learned skill selection, and simulator-grounded skill evolution. We further construct a real-world dataset with 479 expert interaction traces (2507 spans) and 553 memory-dependent evaluation queries covering dispersion engineering, loss optimization, and multi-objective design. Experiments across multiple LLM backbones and classical baselines show that SkillPCF achieves stronger design-quality and efficiency trade-offs under practical simulation budgets, demonstrating the effectiveness of our proposed memory-skill learning paradigm for physics-aware PCF inverse design.

title: HGTFNet: A hybrid graph-enhanced time-frequency network for multivariate short-term electric load forecasting
abstract: Short-term electric load forecasting (STLF) is essential for efficient power system operation, yet existing deep learning models often struggle to simultaneously capture high-frequency transient fluctuations and complex inter-variable dependencies in multivariate load data, leading to over-smoothing and structural distortion. To address these challenges, we propose a Hybrid Graph-enhanced Time-Frequency Network (HGTFNet) that jointly improves numerical accuracy and morphological and spectral fidelity, where fidelity is assessed by waveform morphology (DTW) and harmonic energy distribution (nSpecMAE). HGTFNet adopts a dual-path spectral–temporal architecture that integrates an inverted Transformer backbone with an explicit frequency-domain branch, enabling decoupling of periodic components and stochastic fluctuations while mitigating high-frequency attenuation. A dynamic graph learning module further models cross-variable dependencies to enforce synchronized evolution across multiple load series. In addition, an adaptive temporal query mechanism and a multi-scale convolution module align non-stationary periodic phases and capture fine-grained local variations. Experiments on a real-world urban load dataset (three supply zones) show that HGTFNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple horizons, achieving up to a 21.2% reduction in MAPE compared to iTransformer. Beyond point-wise accuracy, HGTFNet improves fidelity, with up to a 13.7% reduction in DTW and lower nSpecMAE, supported by frequency-domain visualizations. Sensitivity analysis further indicates that performance gains arise from adaptive synergy between temporal and frequency representations rather than any single module. Overall, by effectively alleviating over-smoothing and preserving transient peak dynamics, HGTFNet provides a structurally consistent and robust forecasting solution, offering reliable support for secure grid operation and efficient energy management under complex load conditions.

title: Text-to-seed generation: Training-free open-vocabulary seeded semantic segmentation via re-purposing diffusion as text-guided seed generator
abstract: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) aims to segment image regions corresponding to arbitrary text queries. Although the Segment Anything Model (SAM) is a powerful foundation model for segmentation, its standalone performance on OVSS remains limited. Existing methods therefore often use SAM to refine coarse masks predicted by other models, but this strategy is unreliable when the initial masks are inaccurate. In this work, we argue that more reliable segmentation can be achieved by exploiting SAM as a region expansion module guided by accurate object points (i.e., seeds) rather than inaccurate coarse masks. Inspired by classical seeded segmentation, we reformulate OVSS as text-guided seed localization followed by seed-based region expansion. To realize this idea, we propose Text-to-Seed (T2S), a training-free framework that leverages the text-to-region correspondence of Stable Diffusion to generate attention-based seed points for target categories described by text. These sparse seeds are then used as point prompts for SAM to produce full object masks. Without task-specific training or additional annotations, T2S achieves strong performance on standard OVSS benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of combining semantic grounding with seed-driven spatial segmentation.

title: VARMA-VAE: Stochastic variational forecasting of time series
abstract: This study introduces the VARMA-VAE, a model that integrates interpretable VARMA dynamics with a variational autoencoder. We evaluate it on three real-world datasets (Tesla trading volume, electric production, and NOx emissions) against an LSTM and a Transformer under a controlled shared encoder–decoder setup. The VARMA-VAE matches their point-forecast accuracy on M S E and Q L I K E while outperforming them on C R P S . A component-level ablation against a VAR-VAE variant isolates the moving-average contribution, and a further comparison against a probabilistic Variational Dropout LSTM confirms that the CRPS advantage holds against a fully probabilistic baseline. Unlike prior VAE forecasters such as the Koopman-VAE, TimeVAE, and VRNN, VARMA-VAE yields a closed-form Gaussian predictive distribution whose variance decomposes additively into autoregressive and moving-average components. This combination of accuracy and calibrated uncertainty matters most when forecasts inform risk-sensitive decisions such as seizure detection or heat-wave alerting. Applications span financial markets, operational research, and healthcare.

title: Explainable salary forecasting for recent college graduates: A two-stage machine learning approach with uncertainty quantification
abstract: Rising tuition costs and increasing competition in the graduate job market have intensified the need for accurate, personalized salary forecasts. Existing tools are often overly general and fail to capture the complex interactions among educational, demographic, and employment factors that shape early-career earnings. This study proposes a two-stage machine learning framework that combines salary-bracket classification with continuous regression, using the classification output to refine the prediction space and improve accuracy. Four machine learning models, Random Forest, XGBoost, AdaBoost, and Decision Tree, were trained and evaluated on a nationally representative, multi-year dataset of U.S. college graduates from the National Survey of College Graduates (NSCG, 2003–2019; n = 25,614 ), with hyperparameters optimized via grid search. Random Forest performed best across both stages, achieving a test F1 score of 71.27% for classification and a test R 2 of 74.35% with an RMSE of $13,900 for regression. To quantify predictive uncertainty, conformal prediction intervals were generated using the Model-Agnostic Prediction Interval Estimator (MAPIE) at 70%, 80%, and 90% confidence levels. Model interpretability was addressed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), which identified employment type, employer sector, and degree field as the most influential predictors of early-career salary. The complete framework was deployed as an interactive web application, enabling students and advisors to generate real-time salary predictions with associated uncertainty estimates and feature-level explanations. By integrating predictive accuracy, interpretability, and uncertainty quantification, this work provides a practical and transparent approach to salary forecasting for data-driven career decision-making.

title: Ill-Posedness evolved in the deep: Adaptive Evolutionary Latent Optimization, an application to recovering volatility
abstract: Optimizing complex high-dimensional latent spaces is a fundamental challenge in fields such as quantitative finance, molecular design, and structured data modeling, particularly when addressing ill-posed inverse problems characterized by nonlinearity and implicit input-output relationships. We introduce Adaptive Evolutionary Latent Optimization (AdELO), a novel framework that synergistically combines evolutionary algorithms with generative and objective models to iteratively refine latent space representations and solve complex optimization tasks. AdELO operates by alternating between evolutionary optimization of latent vectors and fine-tuning of both the generative and objective models, effectively navigating the latent space to discover optimal solutions. In our implementation, we utilize beta-Variational Autoencoders (beta-VAEs) to represent the latent space and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to enforce underlying physical laws. We apply AdELO to the recovery of local volatility surfaces from option prices, a quintessential ill-posed inverse problem in financial mathematics known for numerical instability and sensitivity to noise. The volatility surface is parameterized using Gaussian Radial Basis Functions (RBFs) with smoothness priors imposed to regularize the problem. By integrating beta-VAEs and PINNs within the AdELO framework, we effectively reconstruct the local volatility surface from market data. Experimental results demonstrate that AdELO successfully recovers volatility surfaces with high accuracy and stability, mitigating the ill-posedness inherent in the inverse problem. The proposed framework not only advances methodologies for volatility surface recovery but also offers a generalizable optimization paradigm applicable to a wide spectrum of complex, highdimensional problems in science and engineering.

title: From knowledge to rules: Explainable molecular optimization with Large Language Models
Generating knowledge graphs from news articles via multi-agent claim extraction and attribution
abstract: News sources play a fundamental role in democratic societies by shaping how citizens access information about facts, events, and competing viewpoints. It is therefore essential to study how different outlets in different countries fulfil this role. A central aspect of such analyses is the examination of claims expressed by specific voices in the media. However, the large-scale identification, attribution, and extraction of claims from news content remain open challenges, due to the diverse ways in which claims and agents can be expressed, and the distinctive characteristics of journalistic writing. In this paper, we address this challenge by introducing SEER, a comprehensive framework for constructing large-scale knowledge graphs from news articles. To ensure high-fidelity extraction, SEER incorporates a novel Multi-Agent Ensemble module specifically designed to handle the complexity of claim extraction and attribution better than single-model approaches. The resulting knowledge graph is based on an extension of the News Classification Ontology (NCO), which captures the key characteristics of claims in news media. We also present a prototype implementation of the proposed architecture and evaluate it on a corpus of articles drawn from four domains: climate change, UK immigration, the war in Ukraine, and US politics. We perform an evaluation on manually annotated data, showing that SEER’s multi-agent extraction module achieves strong performance (78.22% Macro F1), outperforming ten alternative single-model LLM-based agents on the claim extraction task. We conducted an ablation study and identified recurring error types that highlight remaining challenges in journalistic claim extraction.

title: HBGSA: Hydrogen Bond Graph with Self-Attention for drug-target binding affinity prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target binding affinity accelerates drug discovery by prioritizing compounds for experimental validation. Current methods face three limitations: sequence-based approaches discard spatial geometric constraints, structure-based methods fail to exploit hydrogen bond features, and conventional loss functions neglect prediction-target correlation, a key factor for identifying high-affinity compounds in virtual screening. We developed HBGSA (Hydrogen Bond Graph with Self-Attention), a 3.06M-parameter model that encodes hydrogen bond spatial features. HBGSA uses graph neural networks to model hydrogen bond spatial topology with self-attention enhancement and Pearson correlation loss. Experimental results on PDBbind Core Set and CSAR-HiQ dataset demonstrate that HBGSA outperforms baseline methods with strong generalization capability. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of hydrogen bond modeling and Pearson correlation loss.

R-SVDD: A decentralized radius-aware federated prototype object detection framework
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) methods typically require Deep Neural Network (DNN) weight transfer from FL clients to an FL aggregator (master) for centralized DNN aggregation. However, in real-world settings such as smart-city sensing and emergency-response monitoring, weight transfer may be infeasible due to privacy regulations, operational policies, or unreliable connectivity. In this paper, we present R-SVDD, a fully decentralized FL framework that enables collaborative DNN training for object detection without neural parameter sharing. R-SVDD replaces weight exchange with a lightweight class-wise prototype learning mechanism based on Support Vector Data Description (SVDD), trained locally on object-level detector features at each FL client. Collaboration is achieved by exchanging only SVDD class prototypes in a peer-to-peer topology, allowing event-specific appearance changes observed by one client to propagate as prototype-level adjustments that improve consistency across the federation. To reduce the effect of outlier class summaries under extreme non-IID conditions, R-SVDD introduces a radius-aware filtering rule that uses the SVDD hypersphere radius as a class-wise compactness signal and suppresses prototypes with abnormal class-wise dispersion during aggregation. No DNN weights, gradients, full DNN model updates, or raw training data are exchanged between FL nodes. R-SVDD is evaluated against FedAvg, FedProto, PearFL, and TurboSVM-FL under random multi-client, cross-domain heterogeneous, and Dirichlet non-IID object detection settings. Compared with full-model FL methods such as FedAvg, R-SVDD communicates only one compact center-radius prototype per object class instead of transmitting the complete detector parameter vector. This greatly reduces the exchanged payload while preserving competitive object detection performance against prototype-based FL baselines.

title: Intrinsic-guided hyperspectral semantic segmentation via material-illumination representation learning
PG-LLM-KT: An adaptable prerequisite-guided framework for knowledge tracing with frozen lightweight LLMs
Surveys and artificial intelligence: a new challenge for non-market economic valuation
abstract: The widespread adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents substantial challenges within the field of economics, prompting a discussion on the concepts of homo economicus and machina economicus . The use of AI-generated Silicon samples adds a new dimension to non-market economic valuation. Machina economicus may be capable of articulating preferences and elucidating decision-making processes, evoking human behavior. Discrete choice surveys are nowadays mainly conducted using internet panels, and several concerns have been raised regarding the quality of responses and representativeness of these samples. The main aim of this paper is to analyze preferences from a Silicon sample, and compare the results with a study based on responses of people from an internet sample. The results show that estimates of willingness to pay in the Silicon sample range between 5.34 and 15.70 times those of the internet sample. Silicon samples can be helpful in the initial stages of designing a discrete choice experiment, but they do not replace real people.

title: A taxonomy of interpretable neurosymbolic models for time series classification
abstract: Time series classification (TSC) with deep learning has advanced markedly over the last decade, yet the mechanisms by which models identify and exploit discriminative patterns remain only partially understood, limiting interpretability. This paper surveys neuro-symbolic approaches that aim either (i) to derive knowledge—by extracting human-readable rules and explanations from data—or (ii) to use knowledge—by injecting logical, physical, or structural constraints into learning. We review methods spanning Signal Temporal Logic (STL) formula extraction and temporal decision trees, neuro-symbolic constraint synthesis and circuits, loss-based regularization including physics-informed objectives, probabilistic logic for event reasoning (e.g., DeepProbLog), and concept-level continual learning and distillation. We position these methods along common axes—explicit vs. implicit knowledge, applicability to TSC, capacity for knowledge discovery, prior knowledge requirements, and reproducibility—and discuss typical failure modes, including data bias and reasoning shortcuts. We also relate recent frugalityoriented designs that leverage non-trainable filters without sacrificing accuracy. Our analysis indicates that neurosymbolic techniques can provide actionable explanations and stronger inductive bias, with especially strong results on binary tasks, but face challenges in scaling to multi-class settings, handling shape-dependent phenomena, and ensuring transparent selection of learned rules. The survey offers a taxonomy and practical guidance for integrating symbolic structure with deep learning in TSC, highlighting open problems and promising directions.

title: PAMA: Dual-memory augmentation assisted pseudo-anomaly contrastive learning for multivariate time series anomaly detection
abstract: For multivariate time series anomaly detection, most methods assume that training data are clean and ignore the characteristics of anomalous data. They often suffer from the overgeneralization problem during the reconstruction process. To address these problems, dual-memory augmentation assisted pseudo-anomaly contrastive learning for multivariate time series anomaly detection (shorted as PAMA) is proposed. First, the prior knowledge of anomalies is utilized to generate pseudo anomalies from the original time series. The normal and pseudo-anomalous feature representations that contain global and local information are respectively achieved by the global and local encoders. Two independent memory modules are constructed to further memorize normal and pseudo-anomalous prototypes. Second, a dual-memory augmentation mechanism is proposed to conduct data augmentation upon the normal and pseudo-anomalous feature representations and then obtain the memory-augmented feature representations. Third, the pseudo-anomaly contrastive learning is proposed to perform temporal contrastive learning and instance contrastive learning on the obtained memory-augmented representations. Compared with the fourteen baseline methods, the experimental results demonstrate that PAMA achieves the optimal detection performance.

title: APDRFormer: Asymmetric Perception Decoupling and Recovery Transformer for multi-modal 3D object detection
Seeing the unseen: Cognitive Visual Imagination for camouflaged object detection
abstract: Camouflaged object detection (COD) aims to segment objects that are seamlessly embedded in their surroundings. However, existing models still struggle with extreme camouflage, where local textures are nearly indistinguishable from the background. Motivated by a cognitive analogy, in which observers reduce perceptual ambiguity by imagining a plausible target appearance before verification, we propose a Cognitive Visual Imagination (CVI) framework. CVI is divided into two stages: (1) Mental Template Generation, which uses the generative prior of a frozen pre-trained image editing foundation model to create a cognitive template that highlights the target while suppressing background distractions; and (2) CVINet, a dual-stream segmentation network that combines the original image with the generated template. To bridge low-level visual cues and high-level cognitive priors, CVINet uses a weight-sharing encoder to extract multi-scale features and introduces two modules inspired by complementary perceptual processes: (i) the cognitive semantic injection (CSI) module, which adaptively injects high-level semantic cues based on cross-stream feature discrepancies, motivated by contrastive perception, and (ii) the cognitive structure refinement (CSR) module, which uses high-frequency priors to bolster structural details and refine object boundaries, analogous to boundary confirmation. Extensive experiments with four widely used COD benchmark datasets show competitive performance. By operationalizing a cognitively inspired “imagine-to-verify” workflow, this study provides an effective and practical approach to camouflaged object detection. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

title: Weigh for transfer: Adaptive self-weighted neuron modulation for continual reinforcement learning
A reflection-enhanced LLM literature-to-design framework for surrogate-guided inverse design of high-entropy alloys
SurveyAgent-HKA: A multi-agent framework for scientific survey generation with LLMs and human knowledge augmentation
abstract: Automatic scientific survey generation has become an important task in scientific document processing. The common approach of retrieving literature from a single source (e.g., arXiv) and generating surveys through a one-pass large language model (LLM) call, often leads to limited reference coverage and, more importantly, fails to replicate the expert-driven revision process that is crucial for writing high-quality surveys. In this paper, we introduce a multi-agent framework for improving the quality of end-to-end scientific survey generation with LLMs, augmented by knowledge derived from published surveys and real-world peer review comments of survey papers. The framework decomposes survey generation into a sequence of well-defined sub-tasks, each handled by an LLM-powered agent. A unified literature retrieval pipeline first gathers relevant papers from multiple sources and identifies key topics through clustering, which is then used to generate an initial survey structure. This structure is further refined by incorporating the human-written outline from relevant published surveys. Based on the refined outline, topic-focused papers are collected and re-ranked to select a representative set for drafting a well-grounded survey draft. Then, we identify common issues raised by experts in peer comments from published surveys to guide the revisions and finalize the survey. Experiments on two domains show that our approach outperforms mainstream baselines in citation quality, structural consistency, and content quality. Furthermore, our framework is efficient in both time and cost, making it a practical solution for broader AI-assisted scientific writing applications.

title: Software-defined radio sensing for self-harming behaviour detection using CWT transformation and deep learning
abstract: Self-harming, prevalent among youths and adolescents, is highly linked to coping difficulties, emotional distress, trauma, and low self-esteem. Such behaviors are a serious problem as regards social well-being, mental health and emotional stability, which are detrimental to individuals, society and healthcare systems. Early detection of self-harming behavior is vital for enabling timely intervention and mitigating long-term psychological risks. In this article, we propose an intelligent human self-harming behavior detection system leveraging Software Defined Radio (SDR) signals-based non-contact platform and deep learning. The proposed system uses a multi-carrier orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signal to extract wireless channel state information for self-harm detection. It employs the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) to convert raw one-dimensional (1D) OFDM signals into two-dimensional (2D) spectrogram representations, enriching the feature set for deep learning models. A customised convolutional neural network (CNN) is designed to capture abrupt physical movements associated with self-harm while maintaining low computational complexity for real-time deployment. The customised CNN is rigorously evaluated against benchmark pre-trained deep learning models, including AlexNet, ResNet18, and GoogleNet, to demonstrate competitive sensitivity and specificity. Comprehensive comparisons are conducted based on performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and computational efficiency parameters. The proposed customised model achieves competitive accuracy (96%) and F1-score (94%) while being significantly more computationally efficient, requiring only 3,305,801 trainable parameters, 12.61 MB of memory, and 45.09 ms inference time.

title: CaCoL: Causality-Aware Multi-Centroid Contrastive Learning for multivariate time series anomaly detection
Enhancing large language model-based systems for end-to-end circuit analysis problem solving
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance in data-rich domains such as programming, yet their reliability in engineering tasks remains limited. Circuit analysis, requiring multimodal understanding and precise mathematical reasoning, highlights these challenges. Although Gemini 2.5 Pro has improved capabilities in diagram interpretation and analog-circuit reasoning, it still struggles to consistently solve problems containing both textual descriptions and circuit diagrams. This paper presents an enhanced end-to-end circuit problem-solving framework using Gemini 2.5 Pro as the backbone model for scalable engineering-education applications. We systematically evaluate Gemini 2.5 Pro on undergraduate circuit-analysis problems and characterize two key failure modes: 1) circuit-recognition hallucinations, particularly incorrect source polarity detection, and 2) reasoning-process hallucinations, such as incorrect current direction assumptions. To address recognition errors, we integrate a fine-tuned YOLO detector and OpenCV-based processing to isolate voltage and current sources for polarity re-identification. To mitigate reasoning errors, we introduce an ngspice -driven verification loop that triggers iterative solution refinement with optional human-in-the-loop feedback. On 83 problems, the proposed pipeline achieves 97.59% accuracy versus Gemini’s 79.52% baseline. On four hand-drawn diagram variations, accuracy improves from 60.61%—71.21% to 89.39%—92.42% with statistically significant gains ( p < 0.005 ). An additional evaluation on 43 problems from a different textbook improves accuracy from 58.14% to 83.72%, providing further evidence of cross-textbook generalizability. Error analysis indicates that circuit recognition remains the dominant source of remaining failures, particularly for different diagram representations. These results demonstrate the robustness, scalability, generalizability, and practical applicability of the proposed framework for engineering education and real-world circuit analysis.

title: Self-supervised learning based etching process modeling: Bridging simulation and experimental data
abstract: In the integrated circuit industry, the precise etching process control is critical for realizing the ever scaled new devices. The development of etching process faces new challenges and requires efficient etching simulation to gain insights into the etching mechanisms. This paper introduces a self-supervised learning framework for etching profile prediction, in which a cross convolutional neural network (CCNN) is designed to enhance feature learning. The CCNN incorporates profile-oriented lateral convolution and longitudinal convolution to capture spatial and dynamic variations. The core of our approach lies in self-supervised pretraining: an autoencoder is used as a pretext task to pretrain the lateral convolution layers on simulation data, enabling comprehensive and generalized profile representation. The pretrained representations are then fed to the longitudinal convolution layers, cascade combination layers and fully-connected output layer, which are fine-tuned on experimental data to achieve accurate experimental profile prediction. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the self-supervised learning framework and the CCNN architecture, yielding a reduction in average prediction errors on experimental data from 7.9028 nm to 6.3822 nm. • Bridge the AI modeling gap between simulations and real etching. • Propose an SSL framework for etching modeling. • Introduce CCNN: an SSL friendly network architecture. • MAE is reduced by 19.2% compared with the SOTA CRNN-based method.

title: D2S2-UI: A diffusion-driven synthetic dataset for UAV semantic segmentation and cross-dataset generalization
abstract: High-quality semantic segmentation is essential for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) applications, enabling precise data interpretation and efficient decision-making across diverse domains. However, the development of robust segmentation models is often constrained by the limited availability of large-scale, well-annotated datasets, which are expensive and labor-intensive to produce. In this work, we introduce D²S²-UI, a novel synthetic UAV dataset designed for generalized aerial semantic segmentation. Rather than relying on traditional rendering, our methodology harnesses the vast visual and semantic knowledge priors embedded within large-scale text-to-image diffusion models. By actively guiding these knowledge priors through structured textual conditioning and class-consistent semantic control, our framework synthesizes large volumes of accurately labeled aerial imagery without requiring manual annotation. This knowledge-driven approach allows us to scale dataset creation while ensuring high label fidelity and scene diversity. Specifically, D²S²-UI features multi-altitude (20m, 60m, 120m) and multi-viewpoint (nadir, high-oblique, low-oblique) coverage, alongside systematically injected variations in environmental conditions (e.g., weather, time of day) and region-specific terrains (e.g., Asian, Arabic, American, Egyptian, European). Experimental results demonstrate that models trained on D²S²-UI achieve substantially better segmentation accuracy compared to those trained on existing synthetic UAV datasets, showcasing strong, effective generalization across multiple real-world UAV benchmarks. The dataset is publicly available at https://github.com/fahad-lateef/UAV-semantic-segmentation-dataset to support further research in aerial scene understanding and UAV-based vision systems.

From unimodal to multimodal deep physiological signal analysis in healthcare: A survey of models, fusion and explainability
abstract: Physiological signal analysis supports objective assessment of emotion, stress, pain, and disease progression in healthcare systems. Early research focused mainly on unimodal signals, which perform well in controlled settings but are often affected by noise, limited contextual information and reduced generalisability. Recent advances have shifted towards multimodal deep learning frameworks that jointly exploit complementary physiological signals to improve performance and clinical relevance. This survey provides a comprehensive review of the transition from unimodal to multimodal deep physiological signal analysis in healthcare and systematically examines commonly used physiological modalities, benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics. The survey further analyses multimodal alignment strategies and fusion techniques, covering early, intermediate, and late fusion paradigms, with an application-oriented discussion spanning emotion recognition, stress detection, pain assessment and other related domains. Particular emphasis is placed on explainable artificial intelligence methods for multimodal physiological models, highlighting modality-level attribution, cross-modal interactions and application-specific interpretability. Finally, it discusses key dataset- and method-related limitations, such as data scarcity, class imbalance, fusion complexity and computational constraints and outlines future research directions related to wearable edge intelligence, privacy-aware learning, enhanced data diversity and quantum-inspired approaches. This survey can be used as a structured reference for researchers and practitioners developing trustworthy multimodal deep learning solutions for next-generation healthcare systems.

Stochastic fixed points and Lyapunov exponents: A random dynamical systems theory of hallucination in large language models
